skill.name: edamam-barcode-lookup
skill.description: Look up nutrition facts for a product barcode (UPC/EAN) using the Edamam MCP. Use when the user provides a barcode number (or a photo/scan of one) and wants calories, macros, or full nutrition for that packaged product. Barcode input only — for typed food descriptions or plate photos, this skill is not the right fit.
skill.summary: Retrieve packaged food nutrition from UPC or EAN barcodes through an already connected Edamam MCP.
skill.author: edamam-llc

content.user_title: Look Up Packaged Food Nutrition by Barcode
content.value_statement: A packaged food barcode does not directly show its calories or nutrients. This skill queries Edamam through a connected MCP and summarizes returned nutrition with its serving basis.
actual_capabilities: Accept UPC or EAN digits, remove spaces and dashes, and preserve leading zeros.
Read printed digits beneath a barcode in a photo, requesting typed input when the digits are unclear.
Submit multiple barcodes as separate entries in one connected Edamam MCP call.
Summarize returned product names, calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates while stating the serving basis.
Include additional nutrients, diet labels, and allergen cautions when the response provides them.
Report missing records and connection errors without inventing nutrition values or requesting credentials in chat.
limitations: Requires an already connected Edamam MCP; this skill does not install or configure the connection.
Barcode coverage and available nutrient fields depend on Edamam responses.
Does not analyze typed food descriptions or plate photos; unreadable barcode digits require clarification.
Provides general nutrition information, not medical advice or dietary diagnosis.

use_cases.title: Check a packaged product
use_cases.description: Look up a grocery barcode and review returned calories and macros with the stated serving basis.

use_cases.title: Record nutrition consistently
use_cases.description: Retrieve packaged food nutrients and distinguish per-serving values from per-100-g values before recording them.

use_cases.title: Review several product records
use_cases.description: Submit several barcodes together and summarize returned nutrients, labels, and missing records without filling data gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Look up one barcode
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up barcode [UPC or EAN]. Show the product name, calories, protein, fat, carbohydrates, and serving basis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: retrieve a basic nutrition summary.

prompt_templates.title: Read a barcode photo
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the digits beneath the barcode in this photo and look up its nutrition. Ask me to type any unclear digits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: use a readable photo of a packaged food barcode.

prompt_templates.title: Review multiple products
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up [barcode A], [barcode B], and [barcode C] in one call. Show a table with each returned serving basis and macros.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: summarize several barcode records together.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a detailed nutrition comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up these barcodes: [list]. Remove spaces and dashes; preserve leading zeros. Report returned nutrients, allergen cautions, serving bases, and missing data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review available nutrition fields without assuming equivalent portions.

output_examples.input: Summarize an illustrative result for 000000000000: Example cereal, per 100 g, 380 kcal, protein 8 g, fat 4 g, carbohydrates 78 g.
output: Calories: 380 kcal. Protein: 8 g. Total fat: 4 g. Total carbohydrates: 78 g.

output_examples.input: Look up [barcode] when Edamam returns an empty result.
output_examples.output: Edamam returned no record for this barcode. Please check the printed digits before trying again. No nutrition values are available.

output_examples.input: Look up a barcode when the Edamam MCP is not connected.
output_examples.output: The Edamam MCP is not connected. Complete the one-time setup in the repository README, then try again. Do not share credentials in chat.

best_practices: Provide all printed barcode digits, including leading zeros, and clarify unreadable photos before lookup.
Check the returned product identity and serving basis before comparing or recording nutrient values.
Configure Edamam credentials outside chat and rotate any key accidentally shared in a conversation.
anti_patterns: Submitting food descriptions or plate photos instead of product barcodes.
Inventing nutrition values or treating an unmatched barcode as a product with zero calories.
Pasting API keys into chat or asking the skill to configure MCP credentials.

faq.question: Which barcode formats does this skill use?
faq.answer: It accepts UPC and EAN barcode digits, typically 12 or 13 digits. Spaces and dashes are removed, while leading zeros are preserved.

faq.question: Can I provide a photo of a barcode?
faq.answer: Yes, when the printed digits beneath the bars are readable. If any digits are unclear, the skill asks you to type them.

faq.question: Does it work without an Edamam MCP connection?
faq.answer: No. Connect the Edamam MCP using the repository README before requesting lookups. Credentials must stay outside chat.

faq.question: Can it look up several barcodes together?
faq.answer: Yes. The procedure sends separate barcode entries in one MCP call and summarizes the returned results.

faq.question: What happens when a barcode has no match?
faq.answer: The skill reports that Edamam returned no record and suggests checking the digits. It does not invent nutrient values.

faq.question: Are nutrition values always per serving?
faq.answer: No. Values may be per 100 g or per returned serving. The skill states the response basis and does not assume one.
